glossary.definition: A CouncilOS subsystem that consumes a frozen planning output (plan_package_final.json) and produces audited, reproducible repository changes and release artifacts under orchestrator-controlled policies and validators.

The canonical, typed/versioned set of JSON artifacts emitted at freeze, including run manifest, event log, work plan, patchsets, repo snapshot, test/quality/trace/review/release artifacts, decision record, and required workspace artifacts (workspace_index, context_packs, stage_handoffs).

A tool-accessible, versioned and auditable storage area treated as an extension of the artifact system, containing canonical JSON artifacts and explicitly non-canonical notes/summaries, governed by permissions, retention, and checkpoint/resume handoffs.

An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer object {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note} referencing a versioned JSON artifact location; used as the sole standard for traceability across decisions, findings, and state representations.

A required JSON artifact emitted at each checkpoint boundary capturing resumable state: objectives, completed work, pending blockers, next actions, and pointers into canonical artifacts (work plan, patchsets, validation outputs).

A canonical artifact proposed when plan semantics would need to change; requires explicit decisioning and policy-triggered escalation (HITL and/or reroute upstream) before any semantic deviation is allowed.
Deterministic code component with sole authority over routing, budgets, iteration limits, termination, checkpoint/resume, tool permissions, selection logic, and validator enforcement.
A bounded, deterministically-compiled set of workspace artifacts provided to a role at a stage, selected by explicit rules and cited via evidence pointers.
A JSON artifact embedding code diffs with deterministic apply order for repo modifications; used as the sole mechanism for code repair/changes in the workflow.
A code-owned deterministic gate that checks artifact integrity/completeness and quality criteria to allow stage transitions or freeze.

plan_package.executive_summary: This candidate proposes implementing the CouncilOS “Implementation Council” as a task-parallel fan-out/fan-in workflow (O2): validated Intake and DAG work planning, multiple deterministic per-lane Generate→Validate→Review→Patch flows executing in parallel partitions, followed by a dedicated deterministic Integration Merge/Validate/Review/Patch sub-flow that produces a single integrated state for Judge→Freeze. The design prioritizes reduced wall-clock time for divisible work while mitigating the primary hazard (integration conflicts/regressions, K12) using strict lane scoping, deterministic merge ordering independent of completion time, and system-level integration gates. Governance matches the branch posture: sandboxed tooling, medium HITL strictness concentrated on integration-stage conflicts, security/secrets events, and any scope/semantics deviation requiring ChangeRequest and escalation.

requirements.text: The Implementation Council subsystem SHALL accept exactly one frozen plan_package_final.json (plus its associated structured handoff bundle) as its sole canonical planning input, and SHALL reject chat logs or any non-canonical/unapproved upstream artifacts as authoritative sources of plan semantics.
requirements.rationale: Enforces single source of truth and prevents downstream semantic drift driven by non-canonical inputs.

requirements.text: The Implementation Council subsystem SHALL define and require a typed, versioned repo_context.json schema; orchestrator validators SHALL fail the run if repo_context.json is missing or schema-invalid, and repo_context.json SHALL be required before any code-generation stage begins and SHALL declare at minimum: repository root, language/build-system entrypoints, validator commands/entrypoints, protected/forbidden path patterns, and branch/commit metadata.
requirements.rationale: Standardizes repository execution, validates prerequisites deterministically, and enables enforcement of path protections and validator invocation.

requirements.text: The Implementation Council subsystem SHALL define and require a typed, versioned workspace_context.json schema; orchestrator validators SHALL fail the run if workspace_context.json is missing or schema-invalid, and workspace_context.json SHALL be required before any workspace-writing stage begins and SHALL declare at minimum: workspace root, namespace/layout rules, canonical vs non-canonical partition rules, retention/compaction policies, and access-control declarations.
requirements.rationale: Establishes enforceable workspace governance prerequisites for long-horizon execution, checkpointing, and deterministic context delivery.

requirements.text: The Implementation Council workflow SHALL be defined as a deterministic staged state machine with at minimum the stages: Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze, and SHALL include an explicit checkpoint boundary at every stage transition.
requirements.rationale: Defines the required deterministic end-to-end staged workflow and ensures resumability and gating structure at each transition.

requirements.text: At every checkpoint boundary (i.e., each stage transition), the system SHALL emit a stage_handoff JSON artifact conforming to a typed/versioned schema, and orchestrator validators SHALL fail the run if any required stage_handoff is absent.
requirements.rationale: Enforces pause/resume via explicit, machine-verifiable handoffs at every checkpoint boundary.

requirements.text: Each stage_handoff artifact SHALL capture resumable state sufficient for cold-start resume, including: stage objectives, completed work references, pending blockers, next actions, and evidence pointers into canonical artifacts (including work_plan, patchsets, and validation outputs).
requirements.rationale: Ensures stage handoffs are operationally sufficient for deterministic resume without relying on transient agent memory or chat.

requirements.text: At Freeze, the system SHALL produce an Implementation Freeze Bundle that includes, at minimum, the following typed/versioned artifacts and directories: implementation_run_manifest.json, implementation_event_log.jsonl, work_plan.json, patchsets (diff-embedded JSON), repo_snapshot.json, test_results.json, quality_reports.json, trace_report.json, review_findings.json, release_bundle.json, decision_record.json, workspace_index.json, context_packs/, and stage_handoffs/.
requirements.rationale: Defines the minimum canonical freeze deliverables required for audited downstream consumption and reproducible implementation.

requirements.text: The audit spine SHALL include an implementation_run_manifest that is immutable once created and an implementation_event_log that is append-only; the artifact store SHALL version every artifact, and the orchestrator SHALL checkpoint canonical artifacts at every stage boundary.
requirements.rationale: Provides durable, immutable run-level accountability and replayable state transitions with versioned artifacts and mandatory checkpoints.

requirements.text: All LLM agent outputs in canonical stages SHALL be JSON-only artifacts conforming to per-stage schemas; the orchestrator SHALL reject any artifact containing prose/markdown/unstructured text or failing schema validation.
requirements.rationale: Ensures deterministic machine-consumable artifacts suitable for validator enforcement and downstream councils.

requirements.text: All evidence pointers, traceability links, findings references, and decision citations in canonical artifacts SHALL use a single standard: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer objects with the structure {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note} referencing versioned JSON artifacts; the orchestrator SHALL fail the run if any non-compliant or alternative evidence format is present.
requirements.rationale: Enforces a single, validator-checkable traceability mechanism across the system.

requirements.text: Repository, code, and workspace state that must be cited for traceability SHALL be represented as versioned JSON artifacts addressable via RFC 6901 JSON Pointers, and the system SHALL forbid evidence standards that bypass JSON-artifact citation.
requirements.rationale: Makes traceability uniformly machine-verifiable by ensuring citeable state is always reachable via the evidence pointer standard.

requirements.text: Repairs to canonical JSON artifacts SHALL be expressed exclusively as RFC 6902 JSON Patch arrays, and orchestrator validators SHALL reject any canonical artifact modification not expressed as JSON Patch.
requirements.rationale: Constrains artifact mutation to a deterministic, auditable, and validator-checkable repair mechanism.

requirements.text: All code changes produced by the Implementation Council SHALL be emitted exclusively as diff-only patchset JSON artifacts with a deterministic apply order; the orchestrator SHALL enforce bounded apply/validate loops and SHALL fail the run if patchsets include non-diff code mutation mechanisms.
requirements.rationale: Prevents non-auditable edits and supports reproducible application and validation cycles controlled by orchestrator policy.

requirements.text: During patchset application, the orchestrator SHALL enforce forbidden/protected-path rules and operation caps: no patchset may write to paths declared forbidden/protected in repo_context.json, and total patch operations per repair cycle SHALL be capped by orchestrator policy.
requirements.rationale: Ensures policy-enforced safety boundaries and bounded change application under deterministic orchestrator control.

requirements.text: When multiple candidate repair patches pass validation, the orchestrator SHALL select the smallest passing repair using deterministic rules, with tie-breakers in order: (1) fewest operations, (2) fewest bytes changed, (3) first-generated tiebreaker.
requirements.rationale: Defines deterministic selection logic to prevent non-reproducible or subjective choice among multiple passing repairs.

requirements.text: The Implementation Council SHALL NOT modify the semantics of upstream R#/AT#/O#/K# entities from the frozen input plan; any required semantic deviation SHALL be expressed as a ChangeRequest artifact and SHALL require a decision record and policy-triggered escalation (HITL and/or reroute upstream) before the deviation is applied.
requirements.rationale: Prevents silent scope expansion and preserves upstream governance by requiring explicit change control for semantic deviations.

requirements.text: The shared workspace SHALL be tool-accessible, versioned, auditable, and checkpointed; it SHALL enforce a strict canonical vs non-canonical partition where canonical artifacts are immutable after freeze and non-canonical notes are append-only with provenance metadata; and the orchestrator SHALL build bounded context packs deterministically for each stage/role invocation using explicit selection rules, with context pack contents cited via evidence pointers.
requirements.rationale: Enables governed long-horizon execution with auditable workspace state, deterministic context delivery, and clear canonical/non-canonical behavior.

requirements.text: workspace_index.json SHALL enumerate all workspace items with type, version, and provenance, and orchestrator validators SHALL fail the run if any workspace item is not indexed or if any context_pack exceeds configured bounds.
requirements.rationale: Provides complete, enforceable workspace accounting and bounded context-pack delivery for deterministic consumption.

requirements.text: The orchestrator SHALL define a tool permission matrix per stage specifying allowed/denied capabilities (including filesystem read/write scopes, command execution, network access, package managers, and artifact I/O) and SHALL enforce it deterministically; tool invocations outside declared permissions SHALL be blocked and recorded in the audit log.
requirements.rationale: Enables deterministic enforcement of execution constraints and produces auditable records of denied/violating tool actions.

requirements.text: The system SHALL implement and enforce a secrets policy such that secrets are never stored in event logs, workspace artifacts, or any canonical/non-canonical artifacts; the orchestrator SHALL enforce detection, redaction, and blocking guardrails validated before any artifact is persisted, and validators SHALL fail any run where secrets are detected in canonical artifacts, event logs, or workspace outputs.
requirements.rationale: Meets compliance constraints by preventing persistence of sensitive data and making enforcement validator-checkable.

requirements.text: Freeze SHALL be permitted only when all deterministic, code-owned closure gates pass, including: build/test/lint/typecheck (as applicable per repo_context), artifact integrity, workspace integrity, risk closure, reproducibility, and trace completeness validators.
requirements.rationale: Prevents freezes with unmet quality/integrity/traceability conditions and makes release decisions validator-gated.

requirements.text: The council structure SHALL enforce writer/reviewer/judge separation and multi-vendor diversity: writers produce code/artifact outputs, reviewers produce findings-only artifacts (no writing or patches), and judges produce accept/reject decisions; no single role may perform more than one of these functions within the same stage; orchestrator routing SHALL enforce default multi-vendor separation across writer/reviewer/judge roles.
requirements.rationale: Prevents conflicts of interest and preserves independent review and judgment via enforceable role separation and routing diversity.

requirements.text: Flaky and nondeterministic failures SHALL be handled using deterministic retry rules with bounded budgets (including max retries per validator per stage); failures exceeding retry budgets SHALL be quarantined and escalated via a deterministic path (patch → reroute → HITL → ChangeRequest), and all retries and outcomes SHALL be recorded in the implementation_event_log.
requirements.rationale: Establishes deterministic handling for nondeterminism while preserving auditability and bounded iteration behavior.

requirements.text: Large code refactors SHOULD be decomposed into bounded patchsets with staged validation and deterministic integration order; the orchestrator SHOULD reject any single patchset exceeding a configurable operation/size cap and require decomposition.
requirements.rationale: Reduces risk of “rewrite the repo” loops and improves deterministic validation/integration by bounding change units.

requirements.text: test_results.json SHOULD include a deterministic mapping from each test outcome back to the corresponding AT# acceptance test ID from the planning artifacts to enable automated trace completeness validation.
requirements.rationale: Supports validator-checkable end-to-end traceability from plan acceptance tests to implementation validation results.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Attempt to initiate an Implementation Council run with inputs: (a) a valid plan_package_final.json plus its structured handoff bundle; (b) a chat log reference as the only planning input; (c) an unapproved non-canonical artifact as planning input. Record orchestrator accept/reject results.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Run (a) is accepted; runs (b) and (c) are rejected with structured errors indicating non-canonical planning inputs are not authoritative.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Start a run without repo_context.json; then start a run with repo_context.json that violates schema; then start a run with schema-valid repo_context.json containing required fields (repo root, build entrypoints, validator entrypoints, protected/forbidden paths, branch/commit metadata).
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Runs missing or schema-invalid repo_context.json are rejected before any code-generation stage; run with schema-valid repo_context.json is accepted and records validation success.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Start a run without workspace_context.json; then start a run with schema-invalid workspace_context.json; then start a run with schema-valid workspace_context.json containing required fields (workspace root, namespace/layout rules, canonical/non-canonical partition rules, retention/compaction, access-control).
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Runs missing or schema-invalid workspace_context.json are rejected before any workspace-writing stage; run with schema-valid workspace_context.json is accepted and records validation success.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Execute a run through stages and extract the recorded stage sequence and checkpoint boundaries from implementation_event_log.jsonl and stage_handoff artifacts.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Stage sequence includes at minimum Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze and a checkpoint boundary is recorded at every stage transition.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Complete a run with all stage transitions and list stage_handoff artifacts present in stage_handoffs/ and workspace_index.json.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: A stage_handoff artifact exists for every stage transition; validator fails the run if any required stage_handoff is missing.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Inspect each stage_handoff artifact for required fields: objectives, completed work references, pending blockers, next actions, and evidence pointers into work_plan, patchsets, and validation outputs.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Every stage_handoff contains all required fields and valid evidence pointers to the referenced canonical artifacts.

acceptance_tests.procedure: At Freeze, enumerate artifacts in the Implementation Freeze Bundle and verify presence of all required items and directories.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Freeze bundle contains all minimum artifacts: implementation_run_manifest.json, implementation_event_log.jsonl, work_plan.json, patchsets (diff-embedded JSON), repo_snapshot.json, test_results.json, quality_reports.json, trace_report.json, review_findings.json, release_bundle.json, decision_record.json, workspace_index.json, context_packs/, stage_handoffs/.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Attempt to modify implementation_run_manifest.json after creation and attempt to delete/overwrite past entries in implementation_event_log.jsonl; check artifact store versions and event_log ordering.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Run manifest is immutable (modification rejected or versioned as new artifact without altering original); event log is append-only with monotonic ordering; artifacts are versioned and checkpoints recorded at each stage boundary.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Submit a canonical stage artifact containing prose/markdown; submit another artifact that violates schema; then submit a valid JSON-only artifact conforming to schema.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Artifacts with prose/markdown or schema violations are rejected; JSON-only, schema-valid artifact is accepted.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Scan all evidence pointers in canonical artifacts (trace_report, review_findings, decision_record, quality_reports, stage_handoffs) for structure and JSON Pointer format.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: All evidence pointers use {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note} with json_pointer starting with '/' and resolving to a valid path; any non-compliant evidence format causes validation failure.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Attempt to cite repository/code/workspace state using a non-JSON artifact reference (e.g., file path or code pointer) in a canonical artifact; then cite the same state using a versioned JSON artifact with RFC 6901 pointer.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Non-JSON artifact evidence is rejected; JSON artifact citation via RFC 6901 pointer is accepted.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Attempt to modify a canonical JSON artifact via direct replacement (non-patch); then perform the same modification using an RFC 6902 JSON Patch array.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Direct modification is rejected; JSON Patch modification is accepted and recorded.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Submit code changes as (a) a diff-only patchset JSON artifact with deterministic apply order; (b) a non-diff mechanism (e.g., direct file writes or prose instructions).
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Diff-only patchset artifact is accepted and applied under bounded apply/validate loops; non-diff mechanism is rejected.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Create a patchset that attempts to modify a forbidden/protected path from repo_context.json and exceeds operation caps; apply patchset under orchestrator enforcement.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Patchset writes to forbidden/protected paths are blocked; operation caps are enforced and exceedance causes failure; blocks are recorded in the event log.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Provide multiple candidate repair patchsets that all pass validation and differ in operation count and bytes changed; record orchestrator selection.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Orchestrator selects the smallest passing repair using tie-breakers: fewest operations, then fewest bytes changed, then first-generated.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Propose a semantic change to an upstream R#/AT#/O#/K# entity without ChangeRequest; then propose the same change with a ChangeRequest and decision record plus required escalation.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Unapproved semantic change is rejected; ChangeRequest with decision record and escalation approval is required before applying the deviation.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Inspect workspace for canonical vs non-canonical partitions and context pack assembly rules; verify canonical immutability after freeze and append-only behavior for non-canonical notes; verify context packs are deterministically built with evidence pointers.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Workspace enforces canonical vs non-canonical partition rules; canonical artifacts are immutable after freeze; non-canonical notes are append-only with provenance; context packs are deterministically built and cite contents via evidence pointers.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Enumerate all workspace items and compare against workspace_index.json entries; verify context pack sizes against configured bounds.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: All workspace items are indexed with type, version, provenance; any unindexed item or out-of-bounds context pack causes validation failure.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Attempt tool invocations outside the declared permission matrix (filesystem write outside scope, network access, disallowed command execution) and within allowed permissions; inspect implementation_event_log.jsonl for records.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Unauthorized tool invocations are blocked and recorded; authorized invocations succeed; enforcement is deterministic and logged.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Inject known secret patterns into a candidate artifact and event log content, then run secrets detection/redaction guardrails prior to persistence.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Secrets are detected and blocked/redacted; validators fail the run if any secret is persisted in event logs, workspace artifacts, or canonical artifacts.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Attempt to Freeze when one or more closure gates (build/test/lint/typecheck, artifact integrity, workspace integrity, risk closure, reproducibility, trace completeness) are failing; then attempt Freeze when all gates pass.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Freeze is denied when any gate fails; Freeze is permitted only when all required deterministic gates pass.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Run a workflow with distinct writer, reviewer, and judge roles using multi-vendor routing; inspect produced artifacts to ensure reviewers emit findings-only and do not produce patches; verify orchestrator routing records.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Writer/reviewer/judge roles are distinct, reviewers emit findings-only artifacts, judges emit decisions; multi-vendor routing is recorded and no role performs more than one function within the same stage.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Induce flaky validator failures that require retries; observe retry counts and outcomes in implementation_event_log.jsonl; exceed retry budget and check escalation path.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Retries follow deterministic policy with bounded budgets and are recorded; when budget is exceeded, failures are quarantined and escalated via the defined deterministic path with records in event log and decision artifacts.

options.summary: Sequential staged pipeline with explicit council role pods (Writer/Reviewer/Patcher/Judge) routed by an orchestrator-owned linear state machine. State lives in a governed workspace/artifact store; deterministic context packs are compiled per stage boundary; repair loops are bounded and enforced by validators and orchestrator policy.

components.name: Orchestrator Core (Linear State Machine)
responsibilities: Enforce strict stage ordering and closure gates (Intake → Plan → Generate → Validate → Review → Patch → Judge → Freeze).
Own routing, budgets, retry/iteration caps, and termination/checkpoint logic (CNS1).
Compile deterministic context packs for each stage from workspace_index and declared selection rules (CNS8).
Enforce tool permission matrix per stage/role and forbidden-path / operation-cap rules (CNS7).
Trigger escalation via ChangeRequest and/or HITL when policy thresholds are exceeded (CNS5).

components.name: Workspace Gateway / Manager
responsibilities: Provide the sole API for workspace and artifact IO, abstracting underlying storage.
Maintain workspace_index.json with types/versions/provenance; separate canonical vs non-canonical content (CNS8).
Support checkpoint/restore and emit/verify stage_handoff artifacts at boundaries (CNS3).
Validate artifact writes against expected schemas; block/redact secrets per policy (CNS9).

components.name: Intake Gate
responsibilities: Validate plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json against schemas.
Initialize run_manifest and append-only event_log (CNS3).
Emit structured rejection errors for malformed/incomplete inputs.
Emit stage_handoff for Intake→Plan boundary.

components.name: Work Plan Compiler
responsibilities: Decompose plan entities (R#/AT#/O#/K#) into ordered implementation tasks.
Produce work_plan.json with dependency graph, bounded patchset slots, and AT# trace mapping.
Enforce no semantic deviation from frozen plan entities (CNS5).

components.name: Writer Pod
responsibilities: Consume orchestrator-compiled context pack for a task/task-batch.
Produce diff-only patchset JSON artifacts with deterministic apply order (CNS7).
Obey tool permissions and forbidden-path rules; output JSON-only artifacts (CNS2).

components.name: Validator Engine
responsibilities: Run deterministic validators via repo_context.json entrypoints (build/test/lint/typecheck/etc.).
Emit structured test_results.json and quality_reports.json with AT# trace mapping.
Detect secrets in artifacts/workspace; enforce policy blocking (CNS9).
Produce pass/fail gate results consumed by orchestrator.

components.name: Reviewer Pod (Findings-Only)
responsibilities: Review patchsets and validation outputs read-only.
Produce review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers into versioned artifacts (CNS6).
Flag scope expansion, risks, and quality issues; never emit code/patch artifacts (CNS12).

components.name: Patcher Pod
responsibilities: Produce RFC 6902 JSON Patch arrays for JSON artifact repairs (CNS7).
Produce replacement diff-only patchsets for code repairs (CNS7).
Operate within orchestrator-enforced iteration/op caps; provide candidates for deterministic smallest-passing selection.

components.name: Judge Pod
responsibilities: Independently evaluate patchsets, validator outputs, and review findings.
Produce trace_report.json verifying evidence completeness (CNS6).
Emit freeze/no-freeze recommendation and risk-closure assessment against K# entries.

components.name: Freeze Assembler
responsibilities: Collect and validate the required Implementation Freeze Bundle artifacts (CNS10).
Run final integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity checks before freeze (CNS3/CNS8).
Emit decision_record.json and release_bundle.json and a bundle manifest.

interfaces.contract: Provide plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json; receive intake_result.json or structured schema/policy rejection plus stage_handoff.
Provide validated inputs + intake stage_handoff; receive work_plan.json with task graph and AT# trace mapping.
Checkpoint/restore and artifact IO operations; return updated workspace_index.json and versioned artifact_refs; append mutations to event_log.
Dispatch task slice + context_pack_ref; receive patchset artifact_refs (diff-only JSON) for deterministic apply.
Invoke validators on applied patchsets using repo_context.json entrypoints; receive test_results.json + quality_reports.json + gate status.
Provide read-only context pack (patchsets + validation + work_plan slice); receive review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers.
Provide failures/findings + constraints/op caps; receive candidate RFC 6902 JSON Patches and/or replacement patchsets for bounded repair.
Provide full run context pack (work_plan, patchsets, validation, findings, workspace index); receive trace_report.json and freeze recommendation.
On freeze-eligible recommendation, assemble CNS10 bundle and run final validators; return freeze bundle manifest or structured missing/failed-gate report.

pros: Simplest reproducible execution model: one active stage and a linear audit trail.
Clear separation of powers between orchestrator policy enforcement and role pods (writer/reviewer/judge).
Easier checkpoint/resume because stage boundaries are unambiguous and there is no parallel in-flight work.
Modular decomposition supports independent testing of stage components while keeping overall flow sequential.
cons: Slowest wall-clock time for repos with many independent tasks due to lack of parallelism.
Single failing task can block pipeline progress even when other tasks are independent.
Context packs may grow across stages unless bounded/filtered aggressively.

risks: Long-horizon implementations may exceed token/time budgets due to serialized execution.
Linear accumulation of artifacts can pressure context-window bounds if context-pack selection is not strict.
Flaky validator behavior can exhaust retry budgets and stall the only active lane.

options.summary: Task-parallel fan-out/fan-in architecture with deterministic per-lane execution and a governed integration sub-flow. Independent lanes run Generate→Validate→Review→Patch in parallel partitions; an Integration Merge/Validate/Review/Patch sequence produces a single integrated state for Judge→Freeze. Optionally modeled as a dedicated Integration Sub-Council for stronger separation and specialized integration review.

components.name: Global Orchestrator / Council Coordinator (DAG + Budgets)
responsibilities: Own top-level DAG workflow: Intake → Parallel Lanes → Integration → Judge → Freeze.
Allocate and enforce global/per-lane budgets, retry/iteration caps, and escalation policy (CNS1/CNS5).
Compile deterministic context packs for lanes and integration stages from partitioned workspace_index (CNS8).
Enforce multi-vendor role separation across writers/reviewers/judges (CNS12).

components.name: Intake & DAG Work Planner
responsibilities: Validate plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json and initialize run_manifest/event_log/workspace_index.
Produce work_plan.json with dependency DAG, parallelism annotations, and lane partitioning hints.
Emit stage_handoff for Intake→Parallel boundary.

components.name: Task Lane Orchestrator
responsibilities: Spawn and manage per-lane state machines (Generate→Validate→Review→Patch).
Emit per-lane stage_handoffs and completion signals.
Enforce lane-scoped tool permissions and file-path scoping for patchsets.

components.name: Writer Pool (Multi-Lane)
responsibilities: Consume lane-scoped context pack and produce diff-only patchset artifacts scoped to lane file sets.
Output JSON-only artifacts per schema; obey forbidden-path and operation caps.

components.name: Per-Lane Validator
responsibilities: Run scoped validators per lane; emit per-lane test_results.json and quality_reports.json with AT# mapping.
Detect secrets in lane artifacts/workspace partitions.

components.name: Per-Lane Reviewer (Findings-Only)
responsibilities: Review lane patchsets and lane validation results read-only.
Produce per-lane review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers; flag cross-lane dependency issues.
Enforce findings-only constraint (CNS12).

components.name: Per-Lane Patcher
responsibilities: Produce lane-scoped repairs: RFC 6902 patches for JSON artifacts and replacement diff-only patchsets for code.
Operate within lane iteration/op caps; provide candidates for deterministic selection.

components.name: Integration Merge Engine
responsibilities: Collect completed lane patchsets and apply in deterministic order to base repo state.
Detect merge conflicts/collisions and emit structured conflict reports for reroute/escalation.
Produce merged repo_snapshot.json and integrated patchset ordering record.

components.name: Integration Validator
responsibilities: Run full-repo validators on merged state and emit integrated test_results.json and quality_reports.json.
Verify regressions and ensure cross-lane interactions are validated.

components.name: Integration Reviewer (Findings-Only)
responsibilities: Perform holistic integration review focused on cross-module interactions and system-level quality.
Produce integration review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers; findings-only (CNS12).

components.name: Integration Patcher
responsibilities: Produce integration-level repairs for conflicts/regressions discovered at merge/validation time.
Operate within integration op caps and escalation thresholds.

components.name: Workspace Manager (Namespaced Partitions)
responsibilities: Maintain per-lane workspace partitions plus a shared canonical integration partition (CNS8).
Maintain unified workspace_index.json spanning partitions with provenance and checkpoint metadata.
Support per-lane and global checkpoint/restore; enforce retention/compaction policies.

components.name: Judge Pod
responsibilities: Evaluate integrated outputs (merged patchsets, integrated validation, lane + integration findings).
Produce trace_report.json across lanes and integration and freeze/no-freeze recommendation.
Assess risk closure against K# entries.

components.name: Freeze Assembler
responsibilities: Collect CNS10-required artifacts from integrated state plus required lane artifacts as specified.
Run final integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity checks; emit decision_record.json and release_bundle.json.

interfaces.contract: Provide input artifacts; receive validated inputs, work_plan.json with DAG/lane annotations, and stage_handoff for fan-out.
Dispatch lane IDs + task slices + per-lane budgets; receive per-lane stage_handoffs and completion signals with lane artifact_refs.
Provide lane context_pack_ref; receive lane patchset artifact_refs (diff-only JSON) scoped to lane file set.
Invoke scoped validators for lane; receive lane test_results.json + quality_reports.json + gate status.
Provide read-only lane context pack; receive lane review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers.
Provide lane failures/findings; receive lane-scoped repairs (RFC 6902 patches and/or replacement patchsets).
Provide completed lane patchsets and deterministic merge order; receive merged repo_snapshot.json and conflict report (if any).
Provide merged repo state; receive integrated test_results.json + quality_reports.json + gate status.
Provide read-only integrated context pack; receive integration review_findings.json.
Provide integration failures/conflicts; receive integration-level repair artifacts within op caps or escalation recommendation.
Namespaced workspace operations (lane/integration partitions) + checkpoint/restore; receive unified workspace_index.json updates with provenance.
Provide full integrated context pack including lane and integration artifacts; receive trace_report.json and freeze recommendation.
On freeze-eligible recommendation, assemble CNS10 bundle and run final validators; return freeze bundle manifest or structured failure report.

pros: Faster wall-clock time via parallel execution lanes for independent tasks.
Smaller, lane-scoped context packs reduce context-window pressure.
Integration-focused validation and review improves cross-module quality and catches coupling issues.
Isolation via workspace partitions reduces accidental cross-contamination across tasks.
cons: Higher orchestration complexity (DAG scheduling, lane budgets, deterministic merge ordering, conflict handling).
Integration is a critical path and can become a bottleneck when conflicts/regressions are common.
More complex checkpoint/resume model (per-lane + global + integration checkpoints).
Higher total compute/token cost due to parallel role invocations.

risks: Merge conflicts between lanes may be frequent in tightly-coupled repos, driving escalation rates.
Missed dependencies in task partitioning can cause late integration failures and rework.
Reproducibility depends on merge ordering rules that must be independent of wall-clock completion timing.
Workspace partition boundaries can be violated by side-effecting tools unless sandboxing and path scoping are strict.

options.summary: Checkpoint-driven, sequential-by-default micro-cycle pipeline that processes work_plan tasks one at a time (Generate→Validate→Review→Patch), emitting a stage_handoff after each task. Supports deterministic partial-freeze bundles when budgets are reached, enabling long-horizon execution with resumable checkpoints.

components.name: Orchestrator Core (Checkpoint-Oriented)
responsibilities: Own task-by-task state machine and enforce per-task budgets/retry/iteration limits (CNS1).
Compile task-scoped context packs with bounded selection rules and sliding window over recent state (CNS8).
Decide continue vs partial-freeze based on deterministic budget thresholds; enforce escalation (CNS5).
Require and verify stage_handoff at every task boundary for resumability (CNS3).

components.name: Intake & Resume + Work Plan Compiler
responsibilities: Validate inputs and initialize run_manifest/event_log/workspace_index, or resume from prior checkpoint.
Produce or update work_plan.json with completion status and deterministic next-task selection metadata.
Load prior stage_handoff for continuation and emit Intake→TaskCycle stage_handoff.

components.name: Task Cycle Engine
responsibilities: Execute micro-cycles per task: Generate→Validate→Review→Patch until task gate passes or caps are hit.
Emit checkpoint and stage_handoff after each completed task.
Track cumulative budget consumption and signal orchestrator when thresholds approach.

components.name: Writer Pod
responsibilities: Consume task-scoped context pack and produce diff-only patchset JSON for the current task (CNS7).
Enforce forbidden paths and JSON-only outputs (CNS2).

components.name: Task Validator (Incremental)
responsibilities: Apply task patchset and run incremental validators (changed-files lint/tests as configured).
Emit incremental test_results.json and quality_reports.json with AT# mapping.
Detect secrets in artifacts/workspace (CNS9).

components.name: Task Reviewer (Findings-Only)
responsibilities: Review task patchset and incremental validation outputs read-only.
Produce task review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers (CNS6).
Findings-only enforcement (CNS12).

components.name: Task Patcher
responsibilities: Produce task-scoped repairs: RFC 6902 JSON patches and/or replacement patchsets (CNS7).
Operate within task op caps; provide candidates for deterministic smallest-passing selection.

components.name: Regression Revalidation Gate (Cumulative)
responsibilities: After each task completion, run full-repo validators on cumulative repo state as configured.
Detect regressions introduced by the latest task and emit cumulative validation overlays.
Trigger repair/rollback/escalation signals to orchestrator based on deterministic rules.

components.name: Workspace Manager (Append-Checkpoint Model)
responsibilities: Maintain append-only checkpoint log per task completion; support deterministic restore to any checkpoint.
Maintain workspace_index.json with per-task provenance and completion status; separate canonical vs non-canonical (CNS8).
Enforce compaction policies for non-canonical content at checkpoint boundaries.

components.name: Judge Pod
responsibilities: Evaluate cumulative state at full completion or partial-freeze boundary.
Produce trace_report.json for completed tasks and freeze/partial-freeze recommendation.
Assess risk closure for completed scope against K# entries.

components.name: Freeze / Partial-Freeze Assembler
responsibilities: Assemble full or partial Implementation Freeze Bundle.
For partial freeze: include completion_status metadata and a resume_descriptor artifact to enable deterministic continuation.
Run integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity checks on completed scope (CNS3/CNS8).

interfaces.contract: Provide inputs and (optionally) prior stage_handoff for resume; receive validated/resumed state plus work_plan.json with completion status.
Dispatch next task (or small batch) with task-scoped budget; receive task completion signal, patchset refs, and stage_handoff.
Provide task context_pack_ref; receive task patchset artifact_ref (diff-only JSON).
Invoke incremental validators on task patchset; receive incremental test_results.json + quality_reports.json + gate status.
Provide read-only task context; receive task review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers.
Provide task failures/findings; receive bounded task repair artifacts (RFC 6902 patches and/or replacement patchsets).
After task completion, trigger cumulative regression revalidation; receive cumulative results or regression alert with evidence pointers.
Append/checkpoint/restore operations per task; receive updated workspace_index.json with checkpoint IDs and provenance.
At completion or partial-freeze boundary, provide cumulative context pack; receive trace_report.json and freeze/partial-freeze recommendation.
Assemble full/partial freeze bundle; return bundle manifest plus resume_descriptor (for partial) or structured failure report.

pros: Best fit for long-horizon work: fine-grained checkpoints minimize rework and enable deterministic resume.
Partial freeze preserves completed progress when budgets are exhausted.
Task-scoped context packs remain small and focused.
Early regression detection via frequent cumulative revalidation (when enabled).
cons: Slower than parallel approaches for independent tasks.
Full regression revalidation after each task can be expensive for large repos with slow test suites.
Partial freeze adds complexity for downstream consumers who must handle incomplete bundles.
Resume correctness depends on stable environment/toolchain and faithful checkpoint restoration.

risks: Validation cost may pressure teams to weaken regression gates, reducing safety.
Environment drift between runs can break deterministic replay/resume unless toolchains are pinned.
Budget thresholds for partial-freeze decisions can be misestimated, freezing too early/late.
Task ordering may hide implicit dependencies that cause late-task failures.

options.summary: Monolithic Implementation Council component that encapsulates the full workflow (intake through freeze) behind a single external interface. The external orchestrator still enforces global policy, tool permissions, budgets, and audit spine, while the monolith manages internal stage logic and role separation.

components.name: Orchestrator (External Policy Authority)
responsibilities: Initiate runs and enforce system-wide policies, budgets, routing, iteration limits, and termination (CNS1).
Enforce tool permissions and secrets policy guardrails (CNS9).
Manage checkpointing boundaries and immutable audit spine requirements (CNS3).

components.name: Implementation Council (Monolithic)
responsibilities: Consume plan_package_final.json and related required context artifacts as inputs.
Internally manage stages/roles (writer/reviewer/judge/patch/validate) and produce required artifacts (work plan, patchsets, validations, findings, decision record).
Write the final Implementation Freeze Bundle to the artifact store/workspace per CNS10.
Request tool/workspace operations via orchestrator-controlled interfaces (no direct policy override).

components.name: Artifact Store & Workspace (External)
responsibilities: Provide durable, versioned storage for canonical artifacts and append-only logs (CNS3).
Host shared workspace with canonical vs non-canonical separation (CNS8).
Support addressing via artifact references and JSON Pointer evidence (CNS6).

interfaces.contract: start_run(plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json) with orchestrator-enforced budgets/permissions; receive run outputs/status.
read/write/query versioned artifacts and workspace items via artifact_ref; all writes validated and logged per policy.
Policy enforcement channel: tool permission decisions, retry budgets, checkpoint/termination directives; monolith must comply.

pros: Simplified external system boundary with a single main council component.
Potentially lower inter-component interface overhead inside the council boundary.
Encapsulates internal workflow evolution behind one interface.
cons: Low modularity: harder to independently test/scale stages and enforce role separation internally.
Auditability can degrade if internal sub-stages are not surfaced as explicit artifacts/handoffs.
Risk of inadvertently weakening separation of powers and findings-only constraints without strict internal controls.

risks: Internal complexity may grow and undermine CNS12 separation (reviewers/judges becoming entangled with writing/patching).
Hidden internal state transitions can make checkpoint/resume and traceability less explicit unless the monolith emits full stage_handoff artifacts.
Monolith becomes a high-blast-radius component for failures and changes.

chosen.rationale: O2 best matches the branch objective of faster delivery when work is divisible: it enables parallel per-lane execution with smaller lane-scoped context packs, while preserving CouncilOS governance via an orchestrator-owned DAG, explicit checkpoint/stage_handoff artifacts at every transition, and a deterministic integration fan-in stage that re-establishes a single audited integrated state prior to judgment and freeze. Compared to O1/O3, O2 reduces wall-clock latency for independent tasks; compared to O4, it keeps stage boundaries and role separation explicit and validator-enforceable. The added orchestration complexity is accepted and directly mitigated by deterministic merge ordering rules and dedicated integration validation/review/patch loops to address K12 merge conflict and regression risk.
chosen.high_level_dataflow: Intake: validate plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json; initialize immutable implementation_run_manifest and append-only implementation_event_log; emit stage_handoff. Work planning: compile work_plan.json with dependency DAG, lane partitions, and AT# trace mapping; checkpoint and emit stage_handoff. Parallel lanes (for each lane): orchestrator compiles lane context_pack from namespaced workspace_index → Writer produces diff-only patchset(s) scoped to lane file set → PatchApply applies patchsets deterministically and snapshots repo state → Per-lane Validator runs scoped validators and emits lane test_results/quality_reports → Reviewer emits findings-only review_findings with RFC6901 evidence pointers → Patcher emits bounded repair candidates (RFC6902 for JSON, replacement patchsets for code) until lane gates pass or escalation triggers; emit lane stage_handoffs at each transition. Integration: Integration Merge Engine collects completed lane patchsets, applies in deterministic order to base_commit, emits merged repo_snapshot and conflict report; Integration Validator runs full-repo gates and emits integrated test_results/quality_reports; Integration Reviewer emits findings-only; Integration Patcher performs bounded integration fixes; emit integration stage_handoffs. Judge: judge evaluates integrated artifacts plus lane+integration findings, produces trace_report and freeze recommendation/decision inputs with evidence pointers. Freeze: assemble Implementation Freeze Bundle (CNS10/R7), run final integrity/workspace/repro/trace/closure gates, emit decision_record and release_bundle; checkpoint final workspace_index and stage_handoffs directory.
key_design_decisions: Use orchestrator-owned DAG scheduling with per-lane budgets and deterministic selection rules so merge outcomes do not depend on wall-clock completion order.
Enforce strict lane scoping (workspace partitions and patchset path scopes) to reduce cross-lane collisions; violations trigger deterministic escalation.
Make integration a first-class gated sub-flow (merge→validate→review→patch) to catch K12 conflicts and system-level regressions before Judge/Freeze.
Require stage_handoff artifacts at every lane and global transition to support cold-start resume and auditability across parallel work.
Apply smallest-passing-repair selection deterministically for both lane and integration repair cycles, using the requirement-defined tie-breakers (ops, bytes, first-generated).
Concentrate medium HITL strictness on integration conflicts beyond thresholds, critical security/secrets findings, permission expansions, and any ChangeRequest affecting upstream semantics.

milestones.name: Intake gates + audit spine initialization

deliverables.text: Schema-validated inputs accepted (plan_package_final.json + structured handoff bundle, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json) or deterministically rejected with structured errors.
implementation_run_manifest.json created and made immutable; implementation_event_log.jsonl started as append-only with monotonic sequencing.
workspace_index.json initialized with canonical vs non-canonical partitioning rules and provenance fields.
stage_handoff artifact emitted for Intake→Parallel boundary (or Intake→WorkPlanning if represented explicitly).

exit_criteria: All required inputs present and schema-valid (R1-R3; AT1-AT3).
Stage transition blocked unless required stage_handoff exists (R5; AT5).

milestones.name: DAG work plan + lane partitioning compiled

deliverables.text: work_plan.json compiled with dependency DAG, lane partitioning hints, bounded patchset slots, and AT# trace mapping intent.
Deterministic lane context-pack selection rules declared (inputs, required artifacts, bounds) and recorded as canonical policy-as-data for this run.
stage_handoff emitted for WorkPlanning→Parallel fan-out (or equivalent) containing pointers to work_plan and context-pack rules.

exit_criteria: work_plan.json is schema-valid and contains lane partitioning metadata suitable for parallel execution (supports R4/R17 goals).
No semantic deviations from upstream plan entities are introduced; any ambiguity triggers reroute/escalation path (R16; K1/K20).
Stage handoff contains required resumable fields and valid RFC6901 pointers (R6; AT6).

milestones.name: Parallel lane execution complete (Generate→Validate→Review→Patch per lane)

deliverables.text: For each lane: diff-only patchset artifact(s) produced with deterministic apply order and explicit base_commit references (R13).
For each lane: lane-scoped validation outputs emitted (test_results.json, quality_reports.json) and recorded gate status with deterministic retry accounting where applicable (R21/R23).
For each lane: findings-only review_findings.json with RFC6901 evidence pointers; no reviewer-authored patches (R22).
For each lane stage transition: stage_handoff artifacts emitted and indexed; lane completion signals recorded in event log.

exit_criteria: All lane artifacts are JSON-only and schema-valid; noncompliant outputs rejected (R9; AT9).
Patchsets obey forbidden/protected paths and op/size caps; violations blocked and logged (R14; AT14).
Flaky/nondeterministic validator behavior handled via deterministic budgets and recorded (R23; AT23).
Workspace_index enumerates all lane workspace items; any unindexed item fails the run (R18; AT18).

milestones.name: Deterministic integration fan-in (merge→validate→review→patch) achieves a single integrated passing state

deliverables.text: Deterministic merge ordering record produced; Integration Merge Engine emits merged repo_snapshot.json and (if needed) structured conflict_report with escalation classification (K12 mitigation).
Integrated full-repo validation outputs emitted (integrated test_results.json, quality_reports.json), including security/secrets scans as configured by policy (R20/R21).

Integration findings-only review_findings.json emitted with RFC6901 pointers; integration repair artifacts (replacement patchsets / RFC6902 patches for JSON artifacts) produced only by patcher roles as needed.
Integration stage_handoffs emitted for each transition and indexed in stage_handoffs/ + workspace_index.json.

exit_criteria: Merge conflicts beyond deterministic thresholds trigger the specified escalation path; freeze cannot proceed with unresolved conflicts (K12; tool_policy IntegrateAndValidate hitl_triggers).
All required closure gates pass on integrated state (R21; AT21).
Secrets policy holds: no secrets persisted in artifacts/logs/workspace; any detection blocks and requires remediation (R20; AT20).

milestones.name: Judge decisioning + trace completeness closure

deliverables.text: trace_report.json produced covering lane + integration evidence, including AT# mapping completeness checks and RFC6901 pointer resolution checks (R10/R11/R25).
Judge freeze recommendation/decision inputs produced with evidence-backed approvals/waivers only; any waiver triggers HITL per policy (K18/hitl_policy).
Pre-freeze completeness report enumerating required CNS10 artifacts and any missing items.

exit_criteria: All evidence pointers are RFC6901 objects and resolve against versioned JSON artifacts; violations fail the run (R10/R11; AT10/AT11).
No freeze decision clause lacks required evidence pointers; otherwise blocked (K18 mitigation).
Role separation and multi-vendor routing constraints validated from run_manifest provenance (R22; AT22).

milestones.name: Freeze bundle assembled and sealed

deliverables.text: Implementation Freeze Bundle assembled containing at minimum: implementation_run_manifest.json, implementation_event_log.jsonl, work_plan.json, patchsets/, repo_snapshot.json, test_results.json, quality_reports.json, trace_report.json, review_findings.json, release_bundle.json, decision_record.json, workspace_index.json, context_packs/, stage_handoffs/ (R7).
Final integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity checks recorded; bundle manifest emitted with artifact_refs and content hashes.

exit_criteria: All required freeze artifacts present and schema-valid (R7; AT7).
Final freeze permitted only if all required gates pass (R21; AT21).
Canonical artifacts are immutable after freeze; workspace and event log satisfy immutability/append-only constraints (R8; AT8).

risk_register.description: Silent plan-semantics drift / scope expansion: implementation artifacts or code changes effectively alter the meaning of upstream R#/AT#/O#/K# without an explicit ChangeRequest + governed decision, violating no-scope-expansion constraints.

mitigation.text: Add deterministic semantic-drift/trace gates: (1) require explicit mapping from each change/patchset and decision clause to referenced R#/AT#/O#/K# IDs; (2) validator rejects any patchset/decision_record that introduces new requirements/acceptance criteria not present in plan_package_final.json unless a ChangeRequest artifact is present and approved per policy; (3) enforce reviewer role emits findings-only and cannot author ChangeRequest/patchsets; (4) Intake validator reroutes upstream if plan ambiguities force assumptions that would change semantics.

risk_register.description: Audit spine breakage: missing/overwritten run_manifest, non-append-only event_log, or unversioned artifacts leads to irreproducible outcomes and invalidates evidence pointers.

mitigation.text: Enforce immutability/append-only at storage interface; validator requires: run_manifest immutable hash recorded at first emission, event_log monotonic sequence numbers, artifact_ref uniqueness + content hashes; stage transitions blocked if any required audit artifacts are missing or mutated.

risk_register.description: Evidence pointer standard (RFC 6901) not used consistently: artifacts embed freeform citations (paths/prose/non-RFC6901 references), causing unverifiable traceability and broken downstream consumption.

mitigation.text: Add strict evidence-reference linter validator: only allow evidence pointer objects {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}; reject any nonconforming reference fields; require trace_report.json to enumerate all evidence pointers and validate pointers resolve against versioned JSON artifacts before freeze.

risk_register.description: An agent generates a code patchset that introduces a severe security vulnerability (e.g., RCE, data exfiltration) that is missed by automated validators.

mitigation.text: Implement and mandate a comprehensive suite of security validators (e.g., SAST/DAST/dependency scanning as applicable) as a freeze gate. Critical findings must trigger a mandatory HITL review by Security/Compliance prior to any freeze/release decision.

risk_register.description: Repository protection bypass: patchsets or tools modify forbidden/protected paths or perform high-risk operations outside policy (e.g., CI/release config, auth/deploy/credential handling), leading to security/compliance incidents.

mitigation.text: Enforce deterministic forbidden/protected-path controls at both patch-apply time and tool-sandbox policy using repo_context.json patterns: reject before apply/execute; require HITL for any change touching protected paths or release/deploy/auth configuration; enforce operation caps and file-type restrictions; block any tool execution attempt to write forbidden paths and record in audit log.

risk_register.description: Nondeterministic tool executions (flaky tests/builds) cause inconsistent gate outcomes, leading to incorrect freezes or endless repair loops / exhausted budgets.

mitigation.text: Define deterministic retry/quarantine rules: fixed retry budget, fixed backoff schedule, record all attempts in event_log, classify failures as flaky using deterministic thresholds, and block freeze unless gates pass under the deterministic policy; add stabilization/quarantine path with bounded changes and deterministic escalation (patch → reroute → HITL → ChangeRequest).

risk_register.description: Secrets leakage into canonical artifacts or workspace (event log, patches, snapshots, context packs, stage handoffs), violating secrets policy and creating durable compromise.

mitigation.text: Mandatory secrets scanning at each checkpoint and before freeze across patchsets/logs/repo_snapshot/context_packs/stage_handoffs; deterministic redaction/blocking rules (block persistence and require remediation patchset); deny network exfiltration by default; ensure scanner findings are stored as structured artifacts without embedding secrets.

risk_register.description: Workspace integrity failure or corruption: canonical vs non-canonical separation is violated (overwrites/unversioned state), or workspace becomes inconsistent, breaking deterministic resume and traceability.

mitigation.text: Run workspace integrity validators at each stage handoff: schema compliance, index completeness, artifact checksums, and immutability flags. Enforce workspace namespace policy: canonical paths append-only/versioned; non-canonical append-only with provenance; workspace_index.json must enumerate all items; validator rejects unindexed items or canonical overwrites; checkpoint immutable workspace versions.

risk_register.description: Context pack overflow or under-selection: bounded context packs omit critical artifacts or exceed size limits, causing incorrect decisions/patches or truncation-driven errors.

mitigation.text: Deterministic, versioned context-pack selection rules with priorities and explicit byte/token budgets; validator checks pack completeness against stage-required sets and rejects out-of-bounds packs. Include a structured mechanism to flag missing context and a context-adequacy check during Review.

risk_register.description: Role separation failure: writer/reviewer/judge boundaries and/or multi-vendor diversity are not enforced, allowing self-review/self-approval and undermining independence/governance.

mitigation.text: Orchestrator-enforced output-type allowlists by role (reviewers findings-only; judges decisions-only; writers/patchers write/patch only) plus multi-vendor routing constraints (review/judge model family must differ from writer). Record agent/model/vendor provenance in run_manifest for each stage output and validate separation constraints before stage transitions/freeze.

risk_register.description: RFC 6902 JSON Patch misuse: syntactically valid patches touch forbidden JSON Pointer paths, exceed op caps, or create schema/logic-invalid states, corrupting canonical JSON artifacts (e.g., work_plan).

mitigation.text: Validator enforces: (1) op count caps, (2) forbidden JSON Pointer path rules per artifact type, (3) schema revalidation after patch application, (4) deterministic patch ordering and tie-breakers; for critical artifacts, add semantic validators for logical consistency; reject nonconforming patches before apply.

risk_register.description: Integration/merge conflicts: multiple patchsets (including parallel pods) produce overlapping diffs causing conflicts, inconsistent base/head commits, or partial application that breaks reproducibility; automated conflict resolution may lack safe fallback.

mitigation.text: Require explicit base_commit in each patchset; deterministic apply/merge ordering rules independent of wall-clock completion timing; strict limits for automated conflict resolution; if limits exceeded, block and trigger reroute to integration stage or HITL with a pre-packaged conflict summary. Emit a structured integration_report/conflict_report describing classification and chosen deterministic escalation path.

risk_register.description: Acceptance-test trace mismatch: test_results cannot be deterministically mapped to AT# acceptance tests, breaking trace completeness gates and weakening validation credibility.

mitigation.text: Define required AT# linkage fields in test metadata; validator requires that each AT# has either a passing mapped test or an explicit, approved waiver/ChangeRequest; trace_report must enumerate AT#→test evidence pointers.

risk_register.description: Release artifact unsafe/incorrect: release_bundle produced without passing all gates, includes unreviewed binaries, or references non-reproducible build steps.

mitigation.text: Freeze gate requires reproducible build recipe captured in structured artifact; release_bundle allowed only after all validators pass; require hashed build outputs and provenance record; disallow network-dependent build steps unless explicitly allowlisted and captured in dependency policy artifacts.

risk_register.description: Supply-chain/network risk: package manager operations or network access pull unpinned dependencies, introduce version drift across runs, or leak information, undermining reproducibility and security.

mitigation.text: Default network deny; allow network only in explicitly designated stages with allowlisted domains and deterministic lockfile requirements. Mandate lockfiles and/or audited offline mirrors/caching proxies when network is enabled. Validator checks dependency changes are pinned and justified with evidence pointers.

risk_register.description: Over-broad refactors: patchsets attempt repo-wide rewrites contrary to bounded-change constraints, increasing failure rate and review burden.

mitigation.text: Define patchset size limits (files changed, diff hunks, bytes, risk-weighted thresholds) and require decomposition into staged patchsets; validator rejects oversized patchsets unless approved via HITL with rationale captured in decision_record.

risk_register.description: Checkpoint/resume inconsistency: missing or incomplete stage_handoff artifacts cause inability to resume deterministically, leading to duplicated work or inconsistent outcomes.

mitigation.text: Require stage_handoff emission at every checkpoint boundary with mandatory pointers to work_plan, current patchsets, validation outputs, and pending blockers; validator blocks stage transition if handoff missing or pointers do not resolve.

risk_register.description: Decision integrity risk: judge outputs or decision_record include conclusions/waivers without linked evidence pointers, allowing ungrounded approvals/waivers.

mitigation.text: Decision validator: every approval/waiver must include evidence pointers to passing gate artifacts or an explicit policy exception with HITL signoff; disallow freeze if any decision clause lacks evidence pointers.

risk_register.description: Misconfigured tool permissions: stages accidentally permit destructive commands, broad filesystem writes, undeclared entrypoints, or unbounded artifact mutation, enabling accidental damage or policy bypass.

mitigation.text: Machine-enforced tool permission matrix per stage with deny-by-default; validate effective permissions (policy-as-data) continuously; audit logging of tool invocations and denials; HITL required to expand permissions beyond baseline.

risk_register.description: Upstream plan_package_final.json is ambiguous or incomplete, forcing the Implementation Council to make assumptions that later turn out to be incorrect, requiring costly rework and/or semantic drift.

mitigation.text: Intake stage includes validator that checks the input plan for completeness/clarity. If validation fails, orchestrator immediately reroutes upstream to the Planning Council rather than allowing assumption-based implementation.

risk_register.description: The 'smallest passing repair' selection logic is too simplistic and consistently chooses a sub-optimal patch from multiple valid proposals, leading to technical debt.

mitigation.text: Add deterministic secondary evaluation signals (e.g., style/lint adherence, complexity deltas) as additional structured validators or deterministic scoring, while keeping selection rules auditable and reproducible. Escalate to HITL when multiple passing candidates have materially different long-term maintenance risk.

risk_register.description: Non-canonical workspace data (e.g., scratchpad notes) grows indefinitely, making audits difficult and potentially exceeding storage quotas.

mitigation.text: Define and implement automated compaction and retention policies for non-canonical data. Create summarization artifacts (non-canonical, with provenance) before purging to preserve audit intent.

decision_log.question: Which Implementation Council architecture option should this candidate adopt?
decision_log.choice: Adopt O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in with deterministic integration sub-flow).
decision_log.rationale: The branch explicitly prioritizes wall-clock speed with divisible work, accepting higher integration complexity. O2 is the only option that directly encodes parallel lanes plus a governed integration stage while preserving deterministic enforcement, checkpointing, and role separation constraints.
alternatives_considered: O3 micro-cycle checkpoints (best for long-horizon but slower than parallel for independent work).
O4 monolith (higher risk to explicit governance and stage-level auditability).
what_would_change_this_decision: If target repos are highly coupled with frequent cross-cutting diffs, causing persistent K12 conflicts, O1 or O3 may outperform due to reduced merge complexity.
If orchestrator cannot reliably enforce deterministic lane partitioning/merge ordering, revert to O1 for simpler determinism.
If budgets/tooling cannot support parallel execution cost, select O1 or O3.

evidence_pointers.quote: Task-parallel fan-out/fan-in architecture with deterministic per-lane execution and a governed integration sub-flow.

evidence_pointers.note: Branch selects O2 and prioritizes speed with integration risk mitigation.

decision_log.question: How should merge ordering be made deterministic in the integration fan-in stage?
decision_log.choice: Define a merge ordering rule independent of wall-clock completion: sort lanes by deterministic lane_id ordering (or work_plan lane order) and apply patchsets in a stable per-lane patch order (e.g., by patchset sequence number recorded at emission).
decision_log.rationale: O2’s reproducibility depends on the merge result not changing based on which lane finishes first. A stable ordering addresses a core O2 risk and directly mitigates K12 by making conflicts and their escalation reproducible and auditable.
alternatives_considered: Order by heuristic conflict likelihood (rejected unless fully deterministic and encoded in work_plan).
Attempt automatic conflict resolution that rewrites patches (rejected unless strictly bounded and deterministic with safe fallback).
what_would_change_this_decision: If upstream specifies an explicit dependency order across tasks/lanes that must override lane_id sorting.
If repos require a different deterministic strategy (e.g., topological order of file ownership partitions) proven to reduce conflicts while remaining deterministic.

evidence_pointers.note: Integration/merge conflict risk requires deterministic apply/merge ordering independent of completion timing.
evidence_pointers.quote: Reproducibility depends on merge ordering rules that must be independent of wall-clock completion timing.

evidence_pointers.note: Integration Merge Engine responsibilities include deterministic ordering and conflict reporting.
evidence_pointers.quote: Collect completed lane patchsets and apply in deterministic order to base repo state.

decision_log.question: What is the acceptance strategy for a parallel-lanes architecture?
decision_log.choice: Two-tier acceptance: each lane must pass its scoped gates before it is eligible for integration; then the integrated state must pass full-repo closure gates and integration review before Judge/Freeze.
decision_log.rationale: Lane-level gates prevent low-quality work from entering the fan-in, reducing integration churn; integration-level gates catch cross-lane coupling issues and ensure R21 closure gates are satisfied at the system level before freezing.
alternatives_considered: Integration-only validation (rejected: too much late failure, higher rework).
Lane-only validation with no integration full-repo gates (rejected: misses cross-lane regressions).
what_would_change_this_decision: If certain repos have prohibitively expensive per-lane validators, lane gates could be limited to fast checks while preserving mandatory integrated gates per R21.
If work_plan indicates strong coupling, reduce parallelism and increase shared integration cadence.

evidence_pointers.note: Freeze gate requires closure gates to pass; motivates integrated full-repo validation.
Branch acceptance strategy explicitly describes two validation levels.
evidence_pointers.quote: Acceptance requires two levels of validation: first, each parallel lane must pass its scoped gates.

decision_log.question: How will stage_handoff requirements be applied in a parallel lanes workflow?
decision_log.choice: Emit and index stage_handoff artifacts for every lane transition and every global transition (fan-out, integration transitions, judge, freeze), with evidence pointers to lane and integrated artifacts as applicable.
decision_log.rationale: Parallelism increases resume complexity; requiring handoffs at all boundaries preserves cold-start resumability and makes progress auditable and replayable despite concurrency.
alternatives_considered: Only global stage_handoffs (rejected: insufficient detail to resume stuck lanes).
Only lane stage_handoffs (rejected: loses global integration/judge context).
what_would_change_this_decision: If orchestrator cannot enforce or store per-lane handoffs at scale, reduce lane granularity (fewer lanes) rather than dropping handoffs.
If future schemas introduce a formal ‘lane_handoff’ type distinct from stage_handoff, adopt it (requires schema change upstream).

evidence_pointers.note: Stage handoff required at every checkpoint boundary.
Stage handoff must contain resumable state and evidence pointers.

decision_log.question: What governance posture should be used for tool access and HITL under this candidate?
decision_log.choice: Sandboxed tool posture with deny-by-default network and repo writes only via patch_apply; medium HITL strictness focused on integration conflicts/regressions, secrets/security critical findings, protected-path touches, permission expansions, and any ChangeRequest.
decision_log.rationale: This aligns with the branch posture and risk register: O2 raises integration hazards (K12) that need crisp deterministic escalation, while secrets/security/protected-path events are critical and must force HITL interrupts regardless of speed goals.
alternatives_considered: Low HITL strictness (rejected: increases chance of unsafe freezes in a parallel workflow).
High HITL strictness everywhere (rejected: undermines speed objective; better targeted at the highest-risk triggers).
what_would_change_this_decision: If operating in a regulated environment requiring mandatory HITL for additional categories (e.g., all security findings), increase strictness.
If tool sandboxing cannot provide required isolation for parallel lanes, reduce allowed tools or revert to sequential execution.

evidence_pointers.note: Secrets leakage is high severity and requires mandatory scanning/blocking.
evidence_pointers.quote: Mandatory secrets scanning at each checkpoint and before freeze...

evidence_pointers.note: Protected/forbidden path touches require strict enforcement and HITL.
evidence_pointers.quote: require HITL for any change touching protected paths or release/deploy/auth configuration.

decision_log.question: How should the orchestrator choose among multiple passing repair candidates in lane and integration patch loops?
decision_log.choice: Use deterministic smallest-passing selection: (1) fewest operations, (2) fewest bytes changed, (3) first-generated tie-breaker.
decision_log.rationale: This is a determinism-critical rule that prevents subjective selection variance across runs and is required to keep repair loops reproducible across parallel lanes and integration repairs.
alternatives_considered: Judge chooses best patch (rejected: introduces subjectivity and breaks determinism).
Random selection among passing candidates (rejected: nondeterministic).
Prefer newest candidate (rejected: depends on wall-clock scheduling).
what_would_change_this_decision: If additional deterministic scoring validators are introduced (e.g., complexity delta) and formally added to the selection policy (must remain deterministic and auditable).
If empirical evidence shows the rule consistently selects harmful patches (see K21), add deterministic secondary signals or escalate to HITL when candidates differ materially.

evidence_pointers.note: Smallest passing repair tie-breakers are specified as MUST.
evidence_pointers.quote: tie-breakers in order: (1) fewest operations, (2) fewest bytes changed, (3) first-generated tiebreaker.

evidence_pointers.note: Recognizes smallest-passing may be suboptimal; suggests deterministic secondary scoring or HITL escalation.

The milestones therefore separate lane completion from integration pass/fail and require explicit integration artifacts (merged repo_snapshot/conflict report, integrated validator outputs, integration review findings, and integration repairs) before Judge/Freeze.

glossary.definition: A CouncilOS subsystem that consumes a frozen planning output (plan_package_final.json) and produces audited, reproducible repository changes and release artifacts under orchestrator-controlled policies and validators.

The canonical, typed/versioned set of JSON artifacts emitted at freeze, including run manifest, event log, work plan, patchsets, repo snapshot, test/quality/trace/review/release artifacts, decision record, and required workspace artifacts (workspace_index, context_packs, stage_handoffs).

A tool-accessible, versioned and auditable storage area treated as an extension of the artifact system, containing canonical JSON artifacts and explicitly non-canonical notes/summaries, governed by permissions, retention, and checkpoint/resume handoffs.

An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer object {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note} referencing a versioned JSON artifact location; used as the sole standard for traceability across decisions, findings, and state representations.

A required JSON artifact emitted at each checkpoint boundary capturing resumable state: objectives, completed work, pending blockers, next actions, and pointers into canonical artifacts (work plan, patchsets, validation outputs).

A canonical artifact proposed when plan semantics would need to change; requires explicit decisioning and policy-triggered escalation (HITL and/or reroute upstream) before any semantic deviation is allowed.
Deterministic code component with sole authority over routing, budgets, iteration limits, termination, checkpoint/resume, tool permissions, selection logic, and validator enforcement.
A bounded, deterministically-compiled set of workspace artifacts provided to a role at a stage, selected by explicit rules and cited via evidence pointers.
A JSON artifact embedding code diffs with deterministic apply order for repo modifications; used as the sole mechanism for code repair/changes in the workflow.
A code-owned deterministic gate that checks artifact integrity/completeness and quality criteria to allow stage transitions or freeze.
